Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The test `testNullCommentEqualsEmptyComment` creates three instances of `ZipArchiveEntry` with the same name "foo" but different comments: one with `null`, one with an empty string `""`, and one with "bar". The test asserts that an entry with a null comment should be equal to one with an empty comment.

Looking at the `ZipArchiveEntry.equals` method implementation:
- It first checks if the object references are the same or if the compared object is null or of a different class.
- Then it compares the name strings.
- Next, it compares the comments using a null-safe comparison: if one is null and the other not, it returns false; otherwise it uses `equals` on the comment strings.
- It continues to compare other fields such as time, attributes, method, size, CRC, compressed size, extra fields, and some internal object.

Because the equality check of comments in the `equals` method treats `null` comment and empty string comment as different (null vs ""), those `ZipArchiveEntry` instances are not equal when one has comment `null` and the other has comment `""`.

This matches the issue described where `ZipArchiveInputStream` produces `ZipArchiveEntry` instances with a null comment, and `ZipFile` produces entries with empty string comment, causing them not to be equal and thus not found in a map.

Hence, the root cause is that the `equals` method in `ZipArchiveEntry` distinguishes between null and empty comment, but logically these should be considered equivalent for `ZipArchiveEntry` equality.

This leads to the test failure and the issue that entries from different sources are not considered equal due to null vs empty comment.

Next, I will look if the `hashCode` method has a corresponding issue with comment hashing, and potentially if the comment setting or getting normalizes null and empty strings.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
